summary: Local Health and Wellness profiles a series of relationship workshops that began September 10th, 2023, led by experts in psychology, communication, and holistic health. Seven sessions through November 4th covered communication, empathy, boundaries, trust, conflict resolution, self-care, and intimacy. Each used interactive exercises such as role-play, mock debates, and worksheets to give participants practical tools.
one_line: Local Health and Wellness recaps a 2023 workshop series on healthy relationships covering communication, empathy, boundaries, trust, conflict, self-care, and intimacy.
key_facts: The relationship wellness workshops began on September 10th, 2023 and were highlighted by Local Health and Wellness.
Dr. Samantha Carter, a relationship counselor, spoke on communication on September 15th, stressing openness, honesty, active listening, 'I' statements and non-verbal cues.
Marcus Johnson, a life coach specializing in emotional intelligence, led the empathy session on September 22nd using worksheets and role-playing scenarios.
Marcus Johnson said, "To empathize is to see the world through another's eyes, to feel what they feel, and to let them know they are not alone."
Jessica Liu, a social worker, taught boundaries on October 1st, saying "Boundaries are not walls; they're gates."
Dr. Alex Harmon, a clinical psychologist, led a trust-building seminar on October 7th, describing trust as made of reliability, transparency, and loyalty.
Dr. Alex Harmon said trust is "earned cumulatively, like drops in a bucket, but can be lost in an instant."
Emma Thompson, a mediator with over a decade of experience, led the conflict resolution workshop on October 14th using mock debates.
Emma Thompson named active listening, validating the other person's viewpoint, and finding common ground as the golden rules of conflict resolution, and advised taking a break to de-escalate.
Wellness coach Michael Andrews held a self-care seminar on October 21st, saying "You cannot pour from an empty cup."
Claire Zhang concluded the series on November 4th with a workshop on intimacy and connection, which she described as emotional and intellectual as well as physical.
Claire Zhang suggested hobbies, regular date nights, and distraction-free quality time as ways to build connection.
